column1: # The ways iText's samples and tests open the encrypted PDFs of
# itext-publications-book-java, one line for each way of opening one file,
# read from the classes named above each group. fetch-corpus.ps1 writes these
# lines to _passwords.tsv with the suite's name in front of each file, and
# fetches the certificates, keys and keystores they name.
# A password line gives a password the class holds that PDFBox opens the file
# with, and an empty one besides where the file also opens with none. The
# exceptions are the files of revision 7, which PDFBox refuses before it looks
# at a password: their lines give the password the sample uses. A keystore
# line gives, relative to the suite, the PKCS#12 keystore the sample decrypts
# with and the passphrase that opens it and its key.
# src/main/java/com/itextpdf/samples/book/part3/chapter12/Listing_12_09_EncryptionPdf.java

# Listing_12_11_EncryptWithCertificate.java encrypts for two certificates,
# and its cmp_ files are not opened here. The key of the one whose
# certificate the repository carries, foobar, is in the JKS keystore
# src/main/resources/encryption/.keystore, whose store password f00b4r and
# key password f1lmf3st differ; PDFBox takes one password for both and so
# opens neither way. The other recipient's key is in a store the
# repository does not carry.
